newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM chief says to list base metal futures.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM chief says to list base metal futures.

text.p: The Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) plans to launch futures contracts of key industrial metals -- copper, lead and zinc -- within four to five years, its president said on Wednesday.

"After listing an aluminium futures contract this April, we'll do research on other metal contracts. Copper, lead and zinc will be among our targets," exchange President Naozo Mabuchi told Reuters in an interview.
Mabuchi said the TOCOM had already started research on the base metal contracts, and was unofficially seeking opinions from local trade houses and smelters.
"Some local smelters may not welcome base metal contracts. But establishing a risk-hedging market in a big consuming country like Japan makes sense," Mabuchi said.
"We'll face some repercussions but we would like to launch them within four to five years, if possible," he said.
The TOCOM president also said he was optimistic about the yen-based aluminium contract, which will be listed this April.
He said the exchange would accelerate a publicity campaign aimed at local brokerage houses across the country about the new contract.
The London Metal Exchange (LME), the world's largest metal market, has expressed scepticism about the Tokyo exchange's aluminium contract, citing Japanese aluminium industry opposition.
Ralph Kestenbaum, vice chairman of the LME, sent a letter to Mabuchi last June, expressing doubts about the new contract.

"...to be very honest, I am rather surprised that TOCOM would start an aluminium contract when the Japanese aluminium industry is not wholly in support of this activity," Kestenbaum's letter said. A copy was obtained by Reuters.
"I can only assume that your activities are meant to cover interests which are not really involved in aluminium physical production or consumption or hedging," the letter said.

Mabuchi admitted that the local aluminium industry would not participate in TOCOM's futures contract. "But we're not disappointed, and they may join when the contract shows enough liquidity," he said.
The Tokyo exchange is welcoming overseas participants in aluminium futures, and has received queries from some Asian traders, Mabuchi said. -- Tokyo Commodity Desk +81-3-3432-7391
